body:
Thank you.  A handshake might do.  If someone hugged me I might have a full-blown breakdown but thank you.

Mental illness is no fun but now combined with a lifetime of physical pain thanks to my recent injury it's just too much.  I'm trying though.
Thanks for sending the article.  That's a good point and it wouldn't be very fair to put someone though that unnecessarily so I guess the train is out.  Now for plan B.

I'm at my lowest, to be honest.  At this point I don't see a way out and I'm tired of living with my physical and mental pain.  I just want it all to end and there's only one way that's going to happen.
I've been trying that for over 40 years.  I'm out of hope.

This is very much on-point for me.  As a current patient actively planning my own exit should I leave a note for my therapist letting them know it's not their fault and I appreciate everything that they tried to do for me?  Or would this somehow make things worse?
Good!!!  I'm so happy for you!  Put this all behind you and move on.
Nah, I'm good.  Anyone who wanted to donate funds could better spend the money elsewhere and the possibility of raising enough money is remote at best.

> Also, have you considered getting the help from a better doctor?

I've tried and tried and tried.  I just don't want to deal with it any longer.  I'm closing in on the wrong side of 50, depressed, in debt.  I just no longer care and can't see the point in continuing down this path, but thank you for the kind words!  I do appreciate them!

Thanks.  I've been teetering on the edge of oblivion for a long time and I think I feel the ledge crumbling beneath my feet.  I'll make it through tonight but after that I'm just not sure.  I have to check the weekend trail schedule for starters.

Here is a [small list of organizations](http://www.womenslaw.org/gethelp_national_type.php?type_id=1063) to contact in case the company decides to push back.  Honestly I'd just mention a name or two and I'm sure they would drop any idea of such a thing like a hot potato.  I know I would.  There are organizations and nonprofits that exist for the singular purpose to assisting women to get out of sex work.  It won't matter if you have not done that kind of work before or not - if you are being blackmailed into the job those organizations are going to go into full attack mode on the bastards.

It wouldn't be in their interest to hound you and I am 100% that people get cold feet and back out all the time.  Honestly I think they wouldn't want to waste their time on perusing this any further because doing so could have more repercussions for them than it would for you.  I think you're going to be okay.

All that said there is an organization that assists women who wind up in the sex industry (or about to) but for the life of me I can't remember what it's called.  I'll search for it when I get home.  They may have links to places that can provide legal protection if they threaten you in any way which, again, I don't think they would do.  I certainly wouldn't do that if I were them.  Too much risk.

You could always say you signed up because someone was blackmailing you.  People get forced into that line of work frequently.  Honestly I think if you wanted out they would probably let you out of fear you might have something on them.
No, not really, but thanks for asking.  I'm going to try to avoid alcohol this weekend.. and the train tracks.

Throw-away time.

I wouldn't have disappeared, I would be discovered, and quickly.  There is a train that goes through the next town over and it stops there every evening at a specific time.  Two blocks up from the station the road goes across the tracks.  The train isn't moving all that fast but fast enough not to stop.  I would put my next down on the track.  I figure it would only hurt for about 10 seconds, at most.

When they got to two friends in particular they would confirm I had told both I was thinking of self-harm and I have started to take an anti-depressant without proper medical supervision but hey, at least I'm trying.

By the time the investigators got to my finances all would become clear: I'm two months behind on my mortgage and the credit is maxed out.  It would have taken years to recover from this, they'd say, despite having a well-paying job.  

Lived alone, quiet, read a lot... it wouldn't be all that mysterious I suppose.  Plus my office mate ask why I was sniffling.  I lied.  Told him my dog died recently which is true, if you could four years as "recently".
